note: `keyId` is required — a request naming no key has nothing to act on.
`exportable` is required. Absent must NOT read as a default: the whole point of the member is that the state is stated, and a request that omits it is a producer that has not decided.
`exportable` is a boolean, not a string. `"false"` is truthy in several languages and would invert the request — the most dangerous possible misreading of this task.
Nor a 0/1 integer, for the same reason.
`keyId` must not be empty — the shape a caller lands on when its own key configuration is unset.
No toggle member. The state is absolute so a retry of a lost `false` cannot set `true`; a `toggle` would reintroduce exactly that.

Unknown top-level member is rejected (additionalProperties: false). `reason` is the likeliest to be invented — the justification for a custody change belongs in the producer's own records, not in a member the custodian would have to store and could not verify.
A request must not carry key material. There is no member for it and `ext` is not one.
`ext` keys must be reverse-DNS namespaces (SPEC §4.5.1); a bare word is not one.
